title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Errors & Omissions - Private Settlement
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal makes a severe error on a file. The client offers to sign a waiver agreeing not to sue the paralegal or complain to the LSO, in exchange for the paralegal paying the client $5,000 out of pocket. Can the paralegal ethically agree to this?
options: Yes, settling disputes privately reduces the burden on the courts.
Yes, as long as the paralegal tells the client they have the option to complain.
No, a paralegal cannot privately settle a claim for an error without notifying LawPRO, and any waiver must only follow independent legal advice.
No, errors cannot be compensated with money, only with free legal services.
questions.explain: Rule 3.01 (Competence and Errors). When an error occurs, the paralegal must immediately notify their insurer (LawPRO) and inform the client to get independent legal advice. Privately settling a malpractice claim to avoid LSO scrutiny or without insurer knowledge violates professional duties and voids insurance coverage.
